title: One whole prayer
hookLine: putting it together: dawn prayer, two units, start to finish
tomorrow: When you stop, and start again

cards: It's like learning a song one bar at a time.

Fifteen bars, one a day: the intention, cleanness, a direction, five times, two words that open the door, the standing, the bow, the rising, the prostration, the sitting between, the testimony, the peace to both sides, the count, the schools, and the chair at the back.
Today you hear it played through, once, from the first note to the last. The shortest of the five: dawn, two units. Today: fajr.

teach.h: STILL DARK. WUDU. FACING THE QIBLAH.
teach.b: It's still dark. The sky is only beginning to gray. That's fajr's time.
The person has made wudu, is on a clean spot, facing the qiblah. In the heart, the intention: two rak'ahs of the dawn prayer. Hands rise.
Allahu akbar. The door closes behind. Hands fold, eyes down.
The Fatiha, then a short surah, recited aloud if leading, because the dawn prayer is one of the spoken ones. Allahu akbar, and the bow: glory to my Lord the Great, three times, settled.
Rising: Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You be the praise. Allahu akbar, and down: forehead, nose, hands, knees, toes.
Glory to my Lord the Most High. Up to sit: my Lord, forgive me. Down again, the second prostration.
Allahu akbar, up to stand, and the cycle repeats: Fatiha, a surah, bow, rise, prostrate, sit, prostrate.
Then, instead of standing, the person stays seated for the tashahhud: all greetings are for Allah, peace on the Prophet ﷺ, peace on us and the righteous, finger raised for the witness.
Then blessings on the Prophet and on Ibrahim.
Then right: as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah. Left: the same. And it's over.
Five minutes, maybe less. Before it come two voluntary rak'ahs, which the Prophet said, in Sahih Muslim, are better than the world and everything in it.

teach.h: EVERY PIECE, IN ORDER, BEFORE SUNRISE.
teach.b: Every piece you've learned, in order, before the sun is up.

how: The dawn prayer, fajr, is two rak'ahs prayed between first light and sunrise, recited aloud when leading, and it is preceded by two voluntary rak'ahs, often prayed at home.

o: the night prayer, four units after dark
the dawn prayer, two units before sunrise
the midday prayer said on Fridays

games.q: which words, which moment — tap the pairs.
p: glory to my Lord the Great
peace, to the right and left

s: the dawn prayer is four rak'ahs
fajr is two rak'ahs, the shortest of the five.
the Prophet ﷺ said the two voluntary rak'ahs before fajr are better than the world
better than the world and everything in it (Sahih Muslim).
the dawn prayer is recited silently
it's one of the spoken prayers; the one leading recites aloud.

games.q: you've finished the second prostration of the first rak'ah of fajr. what comes next?
o: sit for the tashahhud and end
stand up for the second rak'ah
games.why: you stand with Allahu akbar and repeat the whole cycle; the tashahhud and the peace come after the second rak'ah.

practice: If you pray, pray the two rak'ahs now, slowly, the way you've learned them, noticing each piece as it passes.

If you don't, walk through the shape without words, standing or in your chair: raise your hands, stand, bow, rise, go down or lean, sit, go down again; then once more, then sit, and turn your head right, and left.

wordCard.voice: Fajr, the two-unit dawn prayer: takbir to taslim, every piece in order, the whole thing played through for the first time.

orig.note: Arabic: the dawn prayer. fajr means dawn, the first break of light.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole thing. Tomorrow: what happens when you stop. Two weeks of prayer, done.
